pointers.sentence: 6.1 came out the next day, on 5 August 2026 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The security archive gives it a patch for each (`docs/releases/security.txt`), and 6.1.1 lists no security fix.
`strip_tags`, and with it the filter `striptags`, can now raise `SuspiciousOperation` (`django/utils/html.py:strip_tags`).
An end tag now pops the stack of open tags only when it closes the tag opened last (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateHTMLParser.handle_endtag`).
At this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).
At this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).

`floatformat` now returns its input as given when the decimal's digits and its exponent's absolute value come to more than 200 (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:floatformat`; [The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md#numbers)).
The number formatter writes a decimal past the same cutoff in scientific notation (`django/utils/numberformat.py:format`).

6.0.8 hands it a `decimal.Decimal`, so a string holding a float gets the locale's format too (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:intcomma`; [Humanize: `naturaltime`, `intcomma` and the other filters](../contrib/humanize.md#the-numbers)).
The guards here stop a long URL before it is split, at `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, 2,048 characters (`django/utils/http.py`).
Python's NFKC normalization, which `urllib.parse.urlsplit` can perform, is slow on Windows (`docs/releases/5.2.12.txt`).
At this commit a word longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH` once its punctuation is trimmed is left as text (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`).
The trimming counts a word's brackets once (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.trim_punctuation`).
By default the widget links only a value `URLValidator` accepts, so none over the bound (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:AdminURLFieldWidget.get_context`).

Each judges its redirect with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses a URL over `MAX_URL_LENGTH` before splitting it (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).

Each judges its redirect with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses a URL over `MAX_URL_LENGTH` before splitting it (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).
It now looks for a scheme only before the first colon (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.to_python`).

`HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__` now raises `DisallowedRedirect`, by default, for a target past `MAX_URL_REDIRECT_LENGTH`, 16,384 characters, before splitting it (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`; [The response object](../http/response.md#redirects)).

Since 5.0.11 and 5.1.5 (CVE-2024-56374), `is_valid_ipv6_address` and, by default, `clean_ipv6_address` refuse text longer than `MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH`, 39 characters, before `ipaddress` parses it (`django/utils/ipv6.py:_ipv6_address_from_str`; [Dates, durations and addresses: `parse_datetime`, `parse_duration` and `clean_ipv6_address`](../utils/parsing.md#ipv6-addresses-clean_ipv6_address)).
It refuses a code with no hyphen there, and any long code when `strict=True` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_supported_language_variant`).

At this commit it refuses a code over the limit before the cache sees it (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:check_for_language`; [Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](../i18n/choosing.md#whether-a-catalogue-exists)).

Under ASGI, `HttpRequest.body` now measures the body as well as checking its Content-Length (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.body`; [The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](../http/body.md#under-asgi)).

`MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input` now judges by the same measure, so by default an upload in a body past that limit goes to disk (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`; [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md#memory-or-disk)).
`ASGIRequest.__init__` now joins its values once (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).
At this commit the parser strips each chunk's white space and joins the pieces once before decoding them (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

Since 6.1 `check_element_type` raises `SuspiciousOperation` where `getInnerText` meets an element with content of its own (`django/core/serializers/xml_serializer.py:check_element_type`; [What changed in caching, files, signals, serialization and pagination](caching-files-signals.md)).

The reader raises `ValueError` past 198, the constant `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS` that is the default of `max_geom_collections=` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).

The reader raises `ValueError` past 198, the constant `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS` that is the default of `max_geom_collections=` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).
At this commit its WKB, from GDAL, is counted at the default, whatever `max_geom_collections=` says (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/geometries.py:OGRGeometry._geos_ptr`).
So a model field given `max_geom_collections=None` still makes a form field that refuses past 198 (`django/contrib/gis/forms/fields.py:GeometryField.__init__`).
